q: Which precise operational definition of 'actually used' interference does Braun & Georgeot use in the Grover asymptote 8 - 24/N? The paper's Sec. IV.F implies restricting the propagator to input |s> = W_n|0> (state-restricted U-tilde), but algebraically stripping W_n from the full unitary gives an asymptote near 4.75, not 8.
basis: My n=3..8 Grover sweep gave I_actually_used in [3.6, 4.9], asymptotically flat as the paper predicts, but ~half the paper's quoted value of 8. The qualitative claim (O(1) asymptote) holds; the quantitative discrepancy is a definitional gap.
next_steps: Implement the state-restricted variant: compute I(P) of the propagator acting only on |s>, using the paper's Eq. 6 with amplitude weights a_i = 1/sqrt(N) fixed rather than the democratic-input Eq. 8. Rerun for n = 3..12 and compare the new asymptote to 8 - 24/N. If it matches, adopt that convention throughout for consistent 'interference budget' accounting.

q: The paper's i-bit convention n_I = log2(I+1) (Sec. IV.A.4) is slipped for the teleportation encoder ('2.58 i-bits' = log2(6)) and Grover asymptote ('3 i-bits' = log2(8)) but should give log2(7) = 2.807 and log2(9) = 3.17 respectively. Is there a physical justification for preferring log2(I) as the 'effective' i-bit count?
basis: My numeric run gave I = 6 exactly for the teleportation encoder, which the definition maps to n_I = 2.807 not the paper's quoted 2.58. Both quotes in the paper agree with each other on log2(I) but disagree with the definition on p.4.
next_steps: Erratum-hunt: check if follow-up papers (Braun 2010+, or citations by van Enk/Rains/Bennett) adopt log2(I) or log2(I+1). Test whether serial-gate composition sub-additivity of n_I is exact under one convention and only approximate under the other.

q: The interference measure I depends explicitly on the computational basis (Sec. IV.C property #3). For Grover, how basis-dependent is the 'actually used' asymptote under Clifford rotations that preserve the oracle's marked-state structure?
basis: My replication used the standard {|0..0>, ..., |1..1>} computational basis. The paper acknowledges basis-dependence but doesn't quantify its effect on the O(1) claim; a rotated basis could in principle change even asymptotic behavior.
next_steps: Numerically sweep Clifford basis rotations U -> C U C^-1 that stabilise the oracle O_marked, evaluate I of (C(DO)C^-1)^k, and check if the O(1) asymptote and the constant (~4.75 in my run, ~8 in paper) are basis-invariants or fluctuate. If fluctuating, define a basis-averaged I* and see if I* has cleaner scaling.

q: The tensor-product identity (N_A N_B - I(A x B)) = (N_A - I(A))(N_B - I(B)) — verified exactly on all 16 pairs I tested — implies the 'IPR mass' N - I is strictly multiplicative under tensor products, a stronger structural fact than the paper flags. Does this give N - I the status of a monotone under some analogue of LOCC?
basis: 16-pair test showed exact multiplicativity to machine precision (residual < 1e-9), not merely additivity of I. The paper only briefly notes I is not additive; the multiplicativity of N - I seems to be lurking unremarked.
next_steps: Formalize: prove (or find a counterexample to) N - I being non-increasing under 'local-only' unitaries U_A x U_B applied post-hoc. If it is, one can define a bipartite 'interference cost' analogous to entanglement of formation. Test on random unitaries and 2-qubit Clifford orbits.

q: The paper's Fig. 4 (Shor, R=15, 12-qubit register) shows accumulated I growing exponentially in the QFT step, but this replication did not run Shor because the intermediate 4096x4096 modular-exponentiation matrices exceed the compute budget for a single subagent turn. Does the paper's Fig. 4 depend on the specific gate decomposition used (e.g. Draper's approximate QFT with phase truncation)?
basis: I reproduced Grover to n=8 exactly but stopped short of Shor. The paper's Shor claim rests on visual inspection of Fig. 4 and one asymptotic formula (2n - 2L); without a rerun we can't cross-check whether the exponential growth kicks in at the same step count.
next_steps: Implement Shor for R = 15 with L = 4 explicitly using Cirq/Qiskit (12-qubit statevector sim is trivial, matrix simulation is memory-tight at 4096^2 complex doubles = 260 MB per matrix but feasible). Compute I at each of the ~60 gates. Cross-check exponential-growth onset step with Fig. 4. Then rerun under an approximate QFT (drop phases below pi/N^2) and see how much I decreases.
